extracted.intended_audience: participants in the Polymath project, complexity theorists and interested researchers discussing the Deolalikar P vs NP paper
extracted.subtask_short: polymath wiki coordination for Deolalikar proof
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for organizing, contributing to, and curating a collaborative Polymath-style wiki to analyze the Deolalikar P != NP paper, including where to post meta-discussion, how to collect resources, and tasks that help the project. Targets coordination of discussion threads, error-tracking, references, and periodic content transfer from blogs to the wiki.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the wiki to collect discussion threads
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect various threads of the discussion on the Deolalikar P != NP paper in the wiki.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seed the wiki with initial discussion points and continue to edit the page as new ideas come up or other discussion appears. The wiki replaces the Google doc because it is easier to edit and better handles many viewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edit the wiki as new ideas appear
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributors should continue to edit the wiki page when new ideas, observations, or discussion arise about the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the wiki up-to-date by folding in relevant comments and new threads; periodic updates and edits are expected as the discussion evolves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect typos and trivial errors separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a section to collect typos and other trivial errors found in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These trivial errors 'do not have much bearing on the essential correctness of the paper' but are useful to document because many eyes are on the paper; such tasks are good wiki work and help engage contributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host main research threads on Lipton/Regan posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the Lipton/Regan blog posts as the primary host for main research threads rather than duplicating them in the wiki.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the blog/wiki distinction: Lipton/Regan posts continue to host main research discussions; the wiki collects, organizes, and curates material, and the blog post can be used for meta-discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use this post for meta-discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the blog post (and by extension the wiki's meta sections) for 'meta' discussions about the project organization and process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As is customary in polymath projects, reserve certain pages/posts for project-level or organizational conversation rather than technical research content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fork discussion threads when unwieldy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a discussion thread becomes too large or unwieldy, create separate forked discussion threads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor thread size (example: the first Lipton post is pushing 117 comments) and split into focused subthreads to keep conversations manageable; transfer content to the wiki periodically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a 'Further reading' section for background resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Compile recommended places to start reading about key concepts (e.g., complexity theory, finite model theory) involved in the discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many commenters asked for reading suggestions; while experts are present, a curated list helps newcomers and should be expanded as long as experts are available to contribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fold relevant external commentary into the wiki
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate important angles and objections raised elsewhere (e.g., error-correcting codes angle, XOR-SAT elaboration, Russell's objections) into the wiki content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture substantive points raised in blog comments and external discussion so the wiki becomes a centralized, organized repository of all pertinent arguments and counterarguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect media/news links under a 'Media' section
rubrics_metrics.description: Link news articles and media coverage related to the paper under a dedicated 'Media' section of the wiki.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid scattering media links; centralize them (the author notes a BBC article is already linked under 'Media') to help track public coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodically transfer curated content from blog/comments to the wiki
rubrics_metrics.description: Move valuable content from blog posts and comment threads into the wiki on a periodic basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the wiki as the canonical, editable collection; transfer and organize material from high-traffic blog posts and comment threads as new content stabilizes or becomes important.
